newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 1996 deficit may hit 3.8 pct GDP-Malan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1996 deficit may hit 3.8 pct GDP-Malan.

text.p: Brazil's public sector operational deficit may go as high as 3.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1996 but will not affect the country's economic growth prospects, Finance Minister Pedro Malan said.
In an interview with newspaper Jornal do Brasil, Malan said he expected the operational deficit to be between 3.5 and 3.8 percent of GDP in 1996 and around 2.5 percent in 1997.
"As we believe that the motor of economic growth is not public spending, it won't be the public deficit that forces us to limit growth," Malan said.

The minister said he expected Brazil's states to show a fiscal improvement because 19 of a total 27 have signed debt renegotiation agreements with Brasilia, obliging them to cut costs, privatize and produce primary surpluses.
The Brazilian government has been gradually revising upwards its forecast of the 1996 public sector deficit.
After an original prediction that the 1996 deficit would be half the five percent shortfall seen in 1995, Malan said in October that the deficit might reach 3.0 percent of GDP.
On Tuesday, ING Barings raised its forecast of Brazil's 1996 public sector operational deficit to 4.5 percent of GDP, up from a previous prediction of 3.5 percent.
The bank said the poor financial situation of the state governments was the main factor driving the deficit.
